findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body:
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. That base class declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:142-164) and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (line 166-170). None of them is implemented here. `Detector.detector_handler` returns `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86). For any detector with type `metric_alert_fire`, that call raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`, and `process_detectors` (processors/detector.py:53) does not catch it. The old stub returned `[]` and did not raise.

I found no non-test caller of `process_detectors` or of `MetricAlertFire`, so nothing breaks today. But the registered group type is now unusable, and a later caller will crash on the first metric-alert detector. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector...` comment on line 10 is also stale now. Either implement the abstract methods with placeholders, or keep the previous non-stateful stub (returning `{}`) until the real implementation lands.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests pass inputs that don't match what they assert
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` takes `value` but never uses it. Several tests exploit that: `test_results_on_change` evaluates with value 100 and `test_dedupe` with value 8, yet both build the expected occurrence with value 6. `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` builds the expected occurrence for group key `val1`, but the result is for `group_key`. These pass only because the mock is insensitive to both. A regression where `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the wrong `value` or `group_key` to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` would go undetected. Have the mock put `value` into `evidence_data` (or the subtitle) and use the real inputs in the expectations.

findings.title: No process_detectors test covers the resolve (StatusChangeMessage) path
findings.body: `process_detectors` now iterates `detector_results.values()` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result`. The new tests only assert `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` for the occurrence case (`PayloadType.OCCURRENCE`). The `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE` branch is not exercised through `process_detectors`. Consider adding a test that goes active, then OK, and asserts the status-change payload is produced.

contracts.action: Detector.detector_handler instantiates MetricAlertDetectorHandler, which is now a StatefulDetectorHandler subclass
contracts.equivalent_path: Test handler MockDetectorStateHandler implements all abstract methods (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:27-39)
contracts.before_after: Before: the stub handler returned [] from evaluate. After: it has abstract methods unimplemented, so instantiation raises TypeError.
contracts.visible_effect: No production caller of process_detectors found, so no user-visible effect yet.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError from group_type.detector_handler(self) at src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86, uncaught in process_detectors (processors/detector.py:53).

contracts.action: process_detectors now consumes a dict of results and produces occurrences for each
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous list-based loop with duplicate group-key detection
contracts.before_after: Duplicate detection is removed. Dict keys by result.group_key make duplicates impossible, and get_group_key_values already returns a dict.
contracts.failure_mode: A custom DetectorHandler returning a dict whose key differs from result.group_key is not checked.

summary: The main problem is `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` in `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`. It now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` without implementing the abstract methods, so instantiating it raises `TypeError`. I found no non-test caller of `process_detectors`, so nothing breaks yet. The processor and model changes look correct. Two test-quality notes remain: the mock occurrence builder ignores its `value` argument, and no test covers the status-change path through `process_detectors`.
